relationship.original_equation: Depreciation fraction = accumulated depreciation / gross PPE

relationship.translation_notes: The fraction is dimensionless; gross PPE need not equal the depreciable base.

variables.definition: Accumulated depreciation divided by gross PPE
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Gross PPE and accumulated depreciation refer to the same asset pool, date, currency and accounting basis.
Amounts are nonnegative magnitudes and gross PPE is positive.
limitations: This is a rough indicator, not an exact proportion of useful life for mixed methods, asset ages or nonzero residual values.
Land, revaluations, impairment and disposals may distort comparisons.

models.summary: The text divides capital expenditure by gross PPE plus capital expenditure as an asset renewal proxy.

relationship.locator: Reading 33, Adjustments related to property, plant and equipment

variables.definition: Capital expenditure divided by gross PPE plus capital expenditure
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Gross PPE and capital expenditure share a currency and relate to the same asset pool.
Gross PPE is measured before the specified additions so adding capex does not double-count them.
limitations: Capex includes additions and growth as well as replacement, so the result is only a renewal proxy.
Cash capex, acquisitions, disposals, construction in progress and gross PPE may cover different asset populations.

variables.definition: Market value divided by tangible book equity
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Market capitalization and tangible book equity cover matching common ownership claims and currency.

limitations: This multiple is not a standalone measure of investment value or a recommendation.
